A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Control-oriented Clustering of Visual Latent Representation. All 33 pages, including Sections 1–6, Appendices A–I, equations, figures and tables, are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulations, NC-pretraining comparisons, and real-world robotic experiments, including Tables 1–3 and the trials in Section 5 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v4 reports the same original simulation and robotic results, including neural-collapse measurements, pretraining comparisons, and real-world trials.

M1.justification: The REPO classification strategies, encoder/decoder architectures, NC pretraining loss, and subsequent behavior-cloning procedure are unchanged (Sections 3–4; Appendices C and F).

E1.justification: Both versions use the same double-integrator example, Lunar Lander, planar pushing and block stacking. Object/domain variations and clean versus visually complex scenarios also remain unchanged, including the appendices.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical: baseline versus NC-pretrained policies in Tables 1 and 3, encoder/decoder variants in Figure 5, and frozen/finetuned, pretrained/random ResNet variants in Table 2.

E3.justification: Demonstration counts, evaluation metrics, test sets and training schedules are unchanged. Appendix F retains the 100-epoch baseline and 50-epoch pretraining plus 50-epoch end-to-end training; Section 5 and Appendix H retain the ten-task real-world evaluations.

E4.justification: The same analyses remain: k-means classification, ImageNet initialization and freezing, continual re-clustering, REPO granularity, decoder variants and weak clustering under limited demonstrations (Appendices B, D, E and G). None is added or removed.

E5.justification: Figures 6 and 21 retain means and standard deviations over three random seeds. Figures 5 and 22 retain single-seed LSTM results. Run-count and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, plotted results and qualitative findings match. For example, both versions report baseline versus NC-pretrained success counts of 5/10 versus 8/10 with clean backgrounds and 6/10 versus 9/10 with complex backgrounds in Section 5.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, neural-collapse metric definitions, REPO construction and mathematical reasoning are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1 contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about control-oriented clustering and NC pretraining, including the claimed 10%–35% test-performance improvement.

C2.justification: Interpretations of re-clustering, ImageNet pretraining and clustering strength are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitation that training requires ground-truth relative poses, making extension to multiple or deformable objects challenging.

D1.justification: Architecture, training, batching and loss details in Appendices A and F are identical, as are the robot hardware and data-collection descriptions in Section 5. The project URL and other access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix I and the research positioning are unchanged, and the bibliography contains the same works. Reference-title capitalization and wrapping changes do not alter cited literature.

P1.justification: v4 adds ICLR 2025 publication text and a reviewer acknowledgment on page 11, adjusts author superscripts, and changes bibliography capitalization. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds a running conference header and horizontal rule, updates the first-page version stamp, and reflows references across pages 11–15. Figures 1–31 and Tables 1–3 retain their content, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: The differences are publication formatting, acknowledgments and bibliography styling. Methods, evidence, explanations, reproducibility details and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. These editorial updates produce no meaningful net change in paper quality.
